## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Its opening canonical verse begins with the phrase *kiccassa kattāraṃ* [Fausböll 1877; Anandajoti 2010].
According to the narrative frame preserved in the commentary, the Buddha related the story while residing at Jetavana with reference to his prominent lay benefactor Anāthapiṇḍika [SuttaCentral]. In the concluding identification of the birth story (*samodhāna*), the Buddha explains the rebirth connections: the ungrateful border merchant (*paccantavāsī*) of the past corresponds to the same borderer in the present, whereas the merchant of Bārāṇasī (*Bārāṇasīseṭṭhī*) was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1877].
No Pali-internal text reuse is reported, and automated analysis via DharmaNexus registers no cross-language alignments with score ≥10 in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral lists no external early parallels, but records four modern translations across four languages [SuttaCentral].
